content.text:
I've read through the code. Here's what's there now, then a plan, then the choices for you.

## What exists today

- **Debts** are stored as `wealth_items` with `kind='debt'`. They count in net worth. You add them by hand on Money → Wealth.
- **Money you lent to someone has no type of its own.** The nearest option is adding it as an "asset".
- **A loan would quietly drop out of net worth.** A wealth item only counts if its "as of" date is today (`app/money/wealth/page.tsx:96`, "Outdated, not in current net worth"). That suits a stock price, but not "Mohammed owes me €500". That amount stays true until something changes it, so it should keep counting.
- **The full chat and the sidebar chat use the same code** (`/api/chat` and `components/chat-messages.tsx`). Building this once covers both.
- **There's already a "propose, then you accept or reject" system.** The agent team uses `agent_proposals` plus `decideProposals` (`lib/ai/agent-apply.ts`). When you accept, it calls the same audited functions you'd use by hand, so history and Undo keep working.
- **Chat can already show custom UI inside an answer.** Charts are drawn from a special code block in the message (`components/ai-message.tsx:47`). A Yes/No card can work the same way.

## Proposed flow (simplest version)

1. You type "I gave 500 EUR to Mohammed". The chat calls a new tool, `iou_propose`. **It saves nothing.** It only creates a pending proposal.
2. The chat shows a card: **"Mohammed owes you €500.00 · since 26 Oct"**, with **[Add] [Edit] [Dismiss]**.
3. Pressing Add creates the record through the normal audited path. It shows up in Wealth and in net worth, and it can be undone.
4. Matching: when money arrives from Mohammed for about that amount (or you pay out, for money you owe), a card appears: **"Mohammed sent you €480 on 2 Nov. Count it against the €500?"**, with **[Settled in full] [Partial €480] [Not this]**. A partial payment lowers what's left, and every change goes into the history.
5. Money you owe works the same way in reverse: "I borrowed 200 from Sara" becomes a debt, and outgoing payments to her are matched.

The matching is plain code that compares names, amounts and dates. The AI only turns your sentence into a proposal. It never decides that a loan has been paid back.

A few decisions change how this gets built:

questions.question: How should 'people owe me / I owe people' be stored?

options.label: Extend Wealth (Recommended)
options.description: Add a 'Lent' kind next to Debt and a 'person' field on wealth items. These stay in net worth until they change. Reuses the current Wealth page, history and Undo. Smallest change.

options.label: New 'People / IOUs' page
options.description: A separate table and page grouped by person, with a running balance per person (lent − repaid). Nicer for many small IOUs, but a lot more new code.

questions.question: Where should the Yes/No cards appear?

options.label: Chat + Home (Recommended)
options.description: Cards show in the chat that made them. Repayment matches also wait on Home, so you see them without opening chat. Reuses the agent proposals system.

options.label: Chat only
options.description: Cards only appear in chat. A repayment match only shows when you ask the chat to check.

questions.question: When should it look for repayments (money from Mohammed, or your payments to someone)?

options.label: Automatically + on ask (Recommended)
options.description: Checks after each bank sync or import and puts suggestions on Home. You can also ask 'did Mohammed pay me back?' in chat.

options.label: Only when I ask in chat
options.description: Simpler. Nothing runs in the background.

questions.question: What counts as a likely repayment?

options.label: Name match, any amount (Recommended)
options.description: The person's name appears in the transaction and the money goes the right way, after the loan date. Amounts close to what's owed are ranked first. Partial payments are caught too.

options.label: Name + amount within ~10%
options.description: Fewer suggestions, but small partial payments won't be suggested.

options.label: Close amount, name optional
options.description: Also catches transfers where the name doesn't show, but you'll get more false matches.

content.text:
Here's the plan with your choices in. Repayment suggestions will show in all three places (chat, Home, and the Agents page), since they all read the same proposals.

## Plan

**1. Data: migration + `lib/schema.ts`**
- Add a `lent` kind to `wealth_items`. The amount must be zero or more, the opposite of `debt`.
- Add an optional `counterparty` field (the person's name) to `wealth_items`.
- Personal `lent` and `debt` items stay in net worth until they change. Other wealth items keep the "today only" rule.

**2. Wealth page**
- Add a "Lent" section and form with a "Person" field. Debts can have a person too.
- Show "Mohammed owes you €500" or "You owe Sara €200".

**3. New proposal types** in `agent-team.ts` and `agent-apply.ts`
- `iou_create`: the person, which way the money went, amount, currency and date.
- `iou_settle`: the item, the matched transaction, and the amount to apply.
- Accepting one calls the same audited wealth save the form uses, so history and Undo work. Rejecting changes nothing.

**4. Chat tools**
- `iou_propose` turns "I gave 500 EUR to Mohammed" into a stored proposal. It can't write anything.
- `iou_findRepayments` handles "did Mohammed pay me back?".
- The chat answer includes a `moneo-proposal` card with Add / Edit / Dismiss, in both the full chat and the sidebar.

**5. Matcher** (plain code, unit-tested)
- Finds transactions that mention the person's name, go the right way (money in for a loan you gave, money out for a debt you owe), and fall after the loan date.
- Amounts close to what's still owed rank first.
- Runs after each bank sync or import as a new agent and creates `iou_settle` proposals, so they show on Home and the Agents page.

**6. Tests**
- Unit tests for the matcher and for applying proposals.
- One end-to-end test: tell the chat about a loan, accept the card, and see it in Wealth and net worth.

Each step gets its own commit, and `npm test`, lint and build run before I finish. Do you want me to start?
